draft.title: Choosing a topic
card: The Personal Interest Project (PIP) is a research project on a topic the student chooses. The first job is to pick a topic that will work well.
Cares about it
the student is interested in the topic, so they can stay motivated through months of research.
Narrow enough
the topic is focused enough to research in depth with the time and resources available. A very broad topic leads to shallow findings.
Linked to the course
the topic connects to Society and Culture concepts, such as culture, identity, social structures or continuity and change, so it can be studied through the course.
draft.remember: A good PIP topic is personal, focused and linked to the course concepts.

a.q: Which PIP topic is narrowest and so best suited to in-depth research?
opts: How social media shapes friendship among teens in one town
How technology has changed the world
How people live in different countries
Why young people are different from older people
a.why: The first topic names one group, one issue and one place, so it can be researched in depth. The others are too broad, and a topic such as how technology has changed the world could never be covered well in a single project.
a.clue: Look for the topic with a clear group, issue and place.

b.q: Ravi loves football and wants a PIP topic. He has narrowed it to how a local junior club shapes the identity of its young players. Which reason best explains why this is a sound choice?
opts: It is focused and linked to the concept of identity
It is popular, so many sources will be available
It is about sport, which is always allowed in the course
It is easy, so no primary research is needed
b.why: Ravi's topic is focused on one club and links to identity, a course concept, as well as his own interest. Being popular or easy does not make a topic good. Interest alone is not enough if the topic does not link to the course.
b.clue: A good topic needs more than interest alone.

a.best: How social media shapes friendship among teens in one town

b.best: It is focused and linked to the concept of identity

problems.detail: The clue 'Look for the topic with a clear group, issue and place' gives the answer away. Only one option names a place ('one town'), so a student can match the clue without understanding why narrowness matters.
The right option is clearly the longest and the only one with precise detail ('among teens in one town'), so it stands out from the three short, vague distractors.

Why (a) calls the right answer 'The first topic', but options are shown in random order. Here it appears last, so the explanation would point students to the wrong option. It should name the topic instead.

opts: How social media shapes friendship among teens in one town
